chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad and Abdullah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, from their father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
Abu Talib professed Islam by the reckoning of al-jummal, and he formed sixty-three with his hand.

key_terms.أَبُو طَالِبٍ: Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.أَسْلَمَ: professed Islam or submitted to Islam
key_terms.الْجُمَّلِ: the numerical system assigning values to letters
key_terms.بِحِسَابِ: by means of reckoning or calculation
key_terms.عَقَدَ: formed or indicated with the hand

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate that Abu Talib had accepted Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith attributes to Abu Talib a declaration of Islam expressed through the numerical reckoning of letters known as hisab al-jummal. It reflects a theological and historical affirmation concerning Abu Talib’s faith within the Shia tradition.
